papers.name: Papers 1 to 4 (all content: Breadth in physics and Depth in physics, Foundation 01/02, Higher 03/04)

topics.name: Chapter P1 Radiation and waves
points: P1.1 The electromagnetic spectrum: wavelength, frequency and energy; speed of EM radiation in space
P1.1 Absorption, transmission and reflection of EM radiation; how radiation is emitted and absorbed by electrons, nuclei and molecules; ionisation
P1.1 Hazards of UV, X-rays and gamma rays; uses of each region of the EM spectrum; radio waves and circuits
P1.2 Radiation emitted by all bodies depends on temperature; radiation balance and the Earth's temperature
P1.3 Describing waves: amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period; transverse and longitudinal waves
P1.3 Wave speed = frequency × wavelength; measuring speed of ripples and sound; ripple tank (PAG4)
P1.3 Reflection and refraction at interfaces; refraction explained by change of wave speed (PAG8)
P1.4 Ray diagrams for reflection, refraction, dispersion and convex and concave lenses (triple)
P1.4 Transmission and absorption at interfaces; colour (triple)
P1.4 Sound in solids and the ear; ultrasound, seismic waves and SONAR to detect hidden structures (triple)

topics.name: Chapter P2 Sustainable energy
points: P2.1 Energy transfer by electric current; power ratings; energy transferred = power × time (J and kWh)
P2.1 Conservation and dissipation of energy; reducing unwanted energy transfers; thermal insulation
P2.1 Efficiency and Sankey diagrams
P2.2 Main energy resources; renewable and non-renewable; generating electricity
P2.2 Mains electricity: a.c. and d.c.; the National Grid and transformers; live, neutral and earth wires
P2.2 Patterns and trends in use of energy resources

topics.name: Chapter P3 Electric circuits
points: P3.1 Static electricity, electron transfer and electric fields (triple)
P3.2 Current as rate of flow of charge; charge = current × time; circuit symbols
P3.2 Resistance and V = IR; investigating resistance of a wire (PAG7)
P3.2 I–V characteristics of resistors, lamps, diodes, LDRs and thermistors (PAG6)
P3.3 Potential difference as work done per unit charge; series and parallel circuits (PAG7)
P3.3 Resistance in series and parallel; sensing circuits with LDRs and thermistors
P3.4 Energy transferred = charge × p.d.; power = p.d. × current = current² × resistance
P3.4 Transformers and why high-voltage transmission is more efficient
P3.5 Magnets, magnetic fields, induced magnetism and the Earth's magnetic field
P3.5 Magnetic field of a current-carrying wire and solenoid; loudspeakers (triple)
P3.6 The motor effect, Fleming's left-hand rule, F = BIl and electric motors
P3.7 Electromagnetic induction; moving coil microphone; alternators and dynamos (triple)
P3.7 Transformers: turns ratio and transformer equations (triple)

topics.name: Chapter P4 Explaining motion
points: P4.1 Forces as interaction pairs; Newton's third law; contact and non-contact forces as vectors
P4.1 Weight = mass × gravitational field strength
P4.2 Speed, typical speeds, measuring speed (PAG3); scalar and vector quantities
P4.2 Acceleration and v² − u² = 2as; investigating acceleration (PAG3)
P4.2 Distance–time and velocity–time graphs, gradients and areas; acceleration in free fall
P4.3 Resultant forces, free body diagrams and scale vector diagrams
P4.3 Momentum, conservation of momentum and change in momentum = force × time
P4.3 Newton's first and second laws; F = ma; inertial mass; circular motion
P4.3 Moments, levers and gears (triple)
P4.3 Reaction times, stopping distances and forces in road safety
P4.3 Estimating stopping distances, accelerations and forces in road vehicles (triple)
P4.4 Work done = force × distance; kinetic and gravitational potential energy
P4.4 Energy transfers in mechanical systems; power as rate of energy transfer

topics.name: Chapter P5 Radioactive materials
points: P5.1 Structure of the atom and development of the atomic model; size of atoms
P5.1 Protons, neutrons and isotopes; nuclear notation
P5.1 Alpha, beta, gamma and neutron emission; balanced nuclear equations
P5.1 Half-life and random decay; activity–time graphs
P5.2 Penetration of alpha, beta and gamma; contamination and irradiation
P5.2 Medical uses of radiation; hazards of ionising radiation and half-life
P5.3 Nuclear fission and chain reactions; nuclear fusion (triple)

topics.name: Chapter P6 Matter – models and explanations
points: P6.1 Density and determining densities of solids and liquids (PAG1)
P6.1 Specific heat capacity and investigating it (PAG5)
P6.1 Specific latent heat; energy calculations when temperature or state changes
P6.2 The particle model: density, changes of state, internal energy and gas pressure
P6.3 Forces causing deformation; elastic and plastic deformation
P6.3 Force–extension, F = kx, work done and energy stored in a spring (PAG2)
P6.4 Pressure in fluids; pressure = force ÷ area; gas pressure and pV = constant (triple)
P6.4 Atmospheric pressure; pressure in liquids, upthrust and floating (triple)
P6.5 The solar system and orbits (triple)
P6.5 Formation of the solar system and the Sun (triple)
P6.5 Red-shift, the expanding universe and the Big Bang model (triple)

topics.name: Chapter P7 Ideas about Science
points: IaS1 Planning investigations: hypotheses, apparatus, variables, sample size, risk and communicating methods
IaS2 Presenting data: units, significant figures, graphs and lines of best fit
IaS2 Analysing and evaluating data: means, ranges, outliers, accuracy, precision, repeatability, conclusions
IaS3 Correlation and cause; how explanations develop over time; peer review; using models
IaS4 Applications, risks and benefits of science and technology; ethical issues; communicating science

topics.name: Chapter P8 Practical skills
points: PAG1 Materials and PAG2 Forces
PAG3 Motion and PAG4 Measuring waves
PAG5 Energy and PAG6 Circuit components
PAG7 Series and parallel circuits and PAG8 Interactions of waves
